keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 1922 but the government was established on 27 May 1921 (infobox; the lead says 'between May 27, 1921 and June 16, 1923'). The page gives no dates for the expansion to Khabarovsk and Spassk; Spassk lies inside the Maritime Province so only Khabarovsk is added. Confidence 2 for the shape.

correction.text: Shape unchanged for 1922, but only until 25 October 1922, when 'the army of the Far Eastern Republic retook Vladivostok'; 1923 is not this shape (see provisional-priamurye-government_1923)

keyframe_review.note: 344,044 km2 for 1922-1923; the infobox gives no area (the Far Eastern Republic's 1.9 M km2 is undated and a different state). The gazetteer reads the shape as the Maritime Province (779 of 783 cells), the southern part of Khabarovsk Krai with Khabarovsk city and the Sovetskaya Gavan coast, and the Ayan coast to 58.1 N: that matches the page's Priamurye enclave plus the Ayano-Maysky District. It cannot hold for 1923: by then only the Ayano-Maysky pocket was left.

correction.text: the Ayano-Maysky District around Ayan on the Sea of Okhotsk, 'controlled by Anatoly Pepelyayev'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the Japanese withdrawal (June to October 1922) the Far Eastern Republic 'retook most of the Priamurye Government territory'; what remained was 'the Ayano-Maysky District', 'controlled by Anatoly Pepelyayev', whose 'surrender in June 1923 marked the end of the Russian Civil War'. The 150 km radius around Ayan is my reading of the district.

region.text: Khabarovsk, 'and then to Spassk' (the page, undated)

ledger.note: 1921: the enclave grows to Khabarovsk. The page: 'Gradually the Priamurye enclave was expanded to Khabarovsk and then to Spassk' and gives no date, so the year is bridged from the enclave's 1922 shape, which reaches Khabarovsk.

region.text: Vladivostok and its Maritime Province, behind a cordon of Japanese troops

ledger.note: 1921, 27 May: a White coup in Vladivostok sets up the Provisional Priamurye Government, 'the last Russian State enclave during the Russian Civil War'. The page: 'The coup was started on May 23, 1921' by the Kappel veterans and the government was headed by the Merkulov brothers 'to survive behind a cordon sanitaire of Japanese troops'; infobox 'Established: May 27, 1921'; the Far Eastern Republic page dates the coup 26 May 1921.

1922, June: Diterikhs replaces the Merkulovs. The page: 'The Merkulovs were deposed in June 1922 by the Priamurye Zemsky Sobor' and 'replaced by one of Admiral Alexander Kolchak's generals, Mikhail Diterikhs'; in July the Zemsky Sobor proclaimed Grand Duke Nikolai Nikolayevich Tsar (neither he nor Patriarch Tikhon attended) and 'the territory was renamed Priamursky Zemsky Krai and Diterikhs styled himself voyevoda'; 'the army was renamed the Zemskaya Rat'. Same state, new regime.

region.text: the enclave without the Ayano-Maysky District, which Pepelyayev kept

ledger.note: 1922, 25 October: the Far Eastern Republic retakes Vladivostok and most of the enclave. The Far Eastern Republic page: the Japanese Army 'announced on 24 June 1922 that it would remove all of its troops from Siberia by the end of October' and 'the army of the Far Eastern Republic retook Vladivostok on 25 October 1922'; the Priamurye page: 'When the Japanese withdrew from the Priamurye (June to October 1922)' the republic 'retook most of the Priamurye Government territory'.

region.text: the Ayano-Maysky District, the last land held

ledger.note: 1923, 16 June: the last White enclave surrenders. The page: infobox 'Disestablished: June 16, 1923'; Pepelyayev's 'surrender in June 1923 marked the end of the Russian Civil War'; infobox 'Succeeded by Soviet Union'.

wars.name: Far Eastern campaign of the Russian Civil War (Priamurye)

zones.text: the Priamurye enclave of 1921-22, with the Ayano-Maysky District to June 1923

wars.outcome: The Far Eastern Republic's army retook Vladivostok on 25 October 1922 after the Japanese withdrawal and Soviet Russia absorbed the republic on 15 November 1922; Pepelyayev surrendered the Ayano-Maysky District in June 1923, 'the end of the Russian Civil War'.
wars.note: The pages give no campaign dates before October 1922 (no Volochayevka, Spassk or Khabarovsk fighting), so the ledger has no contest events; the Priamurye page lists Khabarovsk and Spassk only as places the enclave expanded to.

wars.name: Siberian Intervention (Japanese withdrawal from the Priamurye)
wars.outcome: Japanese troops screened the enclave as 'a cordon sanitaire' and left between June and October 1922; the Far Eastern Republic page: they 'announced on 24 June 1922 that it would remove all of its troops from Siberia by the end of October'.
wars.note: North Sakhalin 'remained under Japanese occupation until 1925' (Far Eastern Republic page) is not Priamurye land; it is carried by the USSR dossier.

certainty.note: An enclave held behind a Japanese cordon, then a coastal pocket; the pages give no boundary line, so all edges are approximate.

sources.title: Provisional Priamurye Government
sources.note: Identity, dates (27 May 1921 to 16 June 1923), capital, leaders, expansion to Khabarovsk and Spassk, Zemsky Sobor, Japanese withdrawal, Ayano-Maysky District and Pepelyayev; no area.

sources.title: Far Eastern Republic
sources.note: The 26 May 1921 coup, the Japanese withdrawal announcement (24 June 1922), Vladivostok retaken on 25 October 1922, absorption into the RSFSR on 15 November 1922; also used by the USSR dossier.

notes:
Pages: 2 (budget 1-2). Cliopatria starts the row in 1922, a year after the government was established (27 May 1921, infobox); a 1921 keyframe is added. The page's dates for the coup differ: 23 May (body), 27 May (infobox, lead), 26 May (Far Eastern Republic page). Cliopatria's shape ends in 1923 with the whole 1922 enclave; the page puts the Soviet retaking of 'most' of it in 1922, so the shape is corrected for 1923 to the Ayano-Maysky pocket.

Not settled: (1) when Khabarovsk and Spassk joined the enclave and when they were lost; (2) where Pepelyayev's seat stood after October 1922; (3) the Zemsky Sobor's exact date (July 1922); (4) whether the pocket stayed attached to the Priamurye government in law (the infobox leader line says 'de facto'). Counterparts: far-eastern-republic and union-of-soviet-socialist-republics have dossiers; empire-of-japan is another group's (jk-01). Gazetteer: all names resolve (Primorye, Vladivostok, Khabarovsk); the Ayano-Maysky District has no gazetteer name, so a coordinate radius is used.
